data.title: US Fintech Weekly: Coinbase Secures Federal Trust Charter, While Hot CPI Pressures Rate-Sensitive Lenders
data.description:
Key points:
  • PayPal partnered with Workday to embed direct deposit capabilities, while Fiserv ended its sixth consecutive week higher. 
  • Shares of SoFi Technologies (SOFI) and Affirm (AFRM) pulled back mid-week after an October Consumer Price Index (CPI) print of 0.4% pushed Treasury yields higher. 
  • Coinbase (COIN) secured final unconditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch Coinbase National Trust Company. 

Fintech stock focused on lending pulled back this week, giving up prior gains as higher-than-expected consumer prices and hawkish commentary from Fed officials sealed expectations for a rate hike in December.

October consumer price index figures outpaced economists' forecasts for the third consecutive month, while producer prices came in a smidge lower than expectations.

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller publicly endorsed a potential half-percentage-point rate hike if inflation momentum persists, a sentiment echoed by Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan and Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee during the week.

Shares of SoFi Technologies (SOFI) and Affirm Holdings (AFRM) ended their second week lower after hot inflation data cemented bets on a Federal rate hike in December. Alternatively, Fiserv (FISV) ended its sixth straight week higher.

Infrastructure Shifts Across Mastercard, Visa And PayPal

Mastercard (MA): The payment company’s shares rose for the sixth consecutive week after Citi raised its share price target on the stock. Citi raised the firm's price target to $800 from $675 and maintained a ‘buy’ rating, which denotes a 21% upside from its Friday closing price.

“MasterCard is well positioned to benefit from its "technology moat" in emerging payment flows,” Citi told investors in a research note accessed by TheFly.

Visa (V): Visa stock also followed its payments peer in recording its sixth week higher on institutional support. Morgan Stanley raised its price target to $471 while maintaining an ‘overweight’ rating on stable earnings growth.

Meanwhile, Citi analysts also raised the target price on Visa to $490 a share. The firm continues to see "durable" sales growth momentum for Visa amid "disciplined" investment returns, citing improving fundamentals and higher peer group multiples for the target boost, as per TheFly.

PayPal (PYPL): PayPal announced a partnership with Workday (WDAY) on Nov. 12 enabling employees at participating companies to set up PayPal Direct Deposit for early paycheck access. Earlier in the week on Nov. 9, subsidiary Venmo introduced an itemized receipt-scanning tool for bill splitting.

Robinhood Sees Strong User Growth, And Coinbase Receives Required Approvals

Robinhood Markets Inc. (HOOD): On Nov. 12, Robinhood reported October operating metrics showing funded customers grew to 28.9 million alongside $15.1 billion in monthly net deposits and a 136% year-over-year surge in event-contract trading volume. Shares traded in an $81.33 to $84.58 range during the week.

Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN): Coinbase announced on Nov. 9 that it received final unconditional charter approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch Coinbase National Trust Company, bringing its institutional digital asset custody operations under direct federal oversight.

Federal Rules And Legal Updates 

The Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) proposed a major board overhaul this week to give Wall Street firms a majority of representation in its oversight for the first time in decades.

Filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the plan would shift the board from a public-member majority—in place since 1996—to a minimum of seven industry governors and at least five public members, while reducing total board seats from 25 to 20.

data.title: Trump to Hold Talks With China's Xi and Russia's Putin Next Week — WSJ
data.description:
By Marianne LeVine and Vera Bergengruen

WASHINGTON- President Trump will meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in China next week for an unprecedented three-way summit, the White House said on Friday.

"The president has made it clear that among other topics he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world," White House spokesperson Olivia Wales said about the meeting, which will be part of the president's trip to the Philippines and China. The meeting will take place Thursday, on the sidelines of the president's visit.

Trump will travel to Asia on Monday and he is scheduled to make a stop in Manila on Tuesday to meet with leaders in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and travel on to China's tech hub of Shenzhen for a meeting with Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders.

The trilateral meeting on Thursday will bring together the leaders of the world's three largest nuclear powers just nine months after the expiration of the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty or New START, the last treaty limiting America's and Russia's strategic nuclear arsenals. Trump has called to replace the agreement with a broader pact that includes Beijing, which has resisted joining arms-control negotiations.

A senior U.S. official said the Trump administration didn't expect to get to any kind of agreement and characterized the leaders' meeting as the first conversation on how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons. The senior U.S. official said that China has the fastest-growing nuclear arsenal of the three powers and that it was time for China to step up about the issue.

Trump intends to discuss the continuing war in Iran with Xi and Putin, the senior U.S. official said, but didn't provide details of what the three leaders intend to accomplish.

The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Putin had floated the idea of a trilateral meeting in a phone call with Trump last month. Trump has publicly indicated that he would be open to the meeting but has said he wanted to discuss denuclearization. After the president's summit with Xi in September, the White House said in a statement that Trump had called for "trilateral arms control negotiations," which China made no mention of in its official readout.

Trump will also participate in a bilateral meeting with Xi, Wales said. It will be the fourth time Trump has met with the Chinese leader in just over a year, and Trump has said they would meet again at the G-20 of major advanced and emerging economies in Miami next month.

Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla and SpaceX will also be with Trump for parts of the China visit, according to the U.S. official. He isn't expected to join the trilateral meeting, the official said. Musk flew with Trump to China on Air Force One during the president's visit to China earlier this year.

The senior U.S. official didn't expect Trump to discuss Ukraine at the trilateral meeting, despite Putin's original proposal to use the event to discuss plans to end the conflict. The prospect of the three leaders meeting to negotiate Ukraine's future without the country's leadership at the table had alarmed officials in Kyiv.

"Inviting Putin to such a meeting would feed his appetite for self-aggrandizement and give him a stature he does not deserve," Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said last month, saying such a meeting would only "encourage Putin to continue this war."

There is no bilateral meeting between Trump and Putin scheduled, the U.S. official said.

data.title: VSAT, AVAV, LMT Secure Multi-Million-Dollar Defense Contracts This Week — But One Stock Stole The Spotlight
data.description:
Despite concerns that Democrats’ midterm election sweep could cloud the outlook for defense spending, defense contractors, including Lockheed Martin (LMT), Viasat (VSAT) and AeroVironment (AVAV), secured multimillion-dollar military contracts this week.

However, the biggest gainer this week was AEVEX (AVEX), which signed a roughly $400-million drone contract.

AeroVironment Bags $720M In New Orders

AeroVironment announced a $405-million international order for its LOCUST X3 laser-defense systems, designed to destroy enemy drones using directed high-energy laser systems. The company highlighted Shahed-series one-way attack drones, which have been frequently used in the ongoing U.S.-Israel-Iran war, as a potential target.

Separately, AeroVironment also secured an initial $315 million U.S. government award under a multiyear contract with a potential value of $940 million. It did not identify the customer or program, citing operational security restrictions.

Viasat, AEVEX Win $400M+ Contracts, ONDS Picks Up Drone Order

Viasat won a $450-million U.S. Space Force contract to develop secure satellite communications infrastructure supporting military operations and the Golden Dome missile-defense initiative. The agreement includes an initial $115 million task order.

Meanwhile, AEVEX (AVEX) announced a multi-year drone contract with a potential value approaching $400 million for unmanned aircraft systems and support services.

On Tuesday, Ondas (ONDS) received an additional military drone order under its Digital Bat program, although financial terms were not disclosed.

Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics And Curtiss-Wright Receive Submarine Contracts

On Tuesday, Curtiss-Wright received contracts worth more than $140 million from General Dynamics Electric Boat to supply propulsion equipment for U.S. Navy Virginia-class and Columbia-class nuclear-powered submarines.

Lockheed Martin (LMT) received an $88.2 million U.S. Navy contract modification for submarine systems engineering and integration. General Dynamics (GD) also secured a $41.6 million contract action for Virginia-class submarine materials and a nearly $20 million award for underwater warfare research.

SpaceX, Parsons In The Spotlight

SpaceX (SPCX) secured a $9.9 million Space Development Agency contract for laser technology research supporting missile tracking, potentially rising to $12.7 million, while Parsons (PSN) announced a $63 million contract to support the National Air and Space Intelligence Center with secure intelligence software.

How Did The Stocks Fare This Week?

AEVEX emerged as the standout performer in the cohort, surging 19% this week, followed by Lockheed Martin, which gained 2.7%, SpaceX, UP 4.2%, and General Dynamics, which edged 0.3% higher. Parsons (PSN) and Viasat (VSAT) traded in the red, declining 3.15% and 4.2%, respectively.

Year to date, Viasat shares have surged more than double, outperforming Lockheed Martin’s 25% gain and General Dynamics’ 7.8% rise. Among the decliners, Parsons has shed 19.3%, AEVEX is down nearly 49%, while AeroVironment has slumped 53%.

data.title: The Weekly Spread: What Shaped US Treasury Yields And The Dollar This Week
data.description:
Key points:
  • A post-election bond rally was cut short this week as stubborn consumer price data and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary weighed on sentiment. 
  • Driven by fears of impending monetary tightening, 2-year Treasury yields surged 35 basis points for the week, while 10-year yields climbed nearly 30 basis points to settle at 5.14%. 
  • The Dollar Spot Index advanced 0.7% to notch its best week since October 2. 

U.S. bond prices reversed last week’s gains across tenures during the week ending November 13, as mounting evidence of persistent inflation shattered hopes that the post-election bond rally would mark the end of the year's debt rout.

After a political shift in Washington during the mid-term elections sparked an enthusiastic flight-to-quality into sovereign debt, fixed-income investors were confronted with a harsh macroeconomic reality of stubborn price pressures and increasingly hawkish rhetoric from Federal Reserve officials during the week ending November 13.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield broke past the 5.00% threshold for the first time since the week ending October 26. U.S. two-year Treasury yields skyrocketed 35 basis points over the five sessions—marking their most dramatic weekly surge in over two years

The spread between the U.S. 10-year yield and the U.S. 2-year yield ticked lower by 7 basis points to 0.28% in the week.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury ETF (TLT) ended its worst week since April 2025, dropping over 3% this week, while the shorter-duration iShares 1-3 year ETF (SHY) eased slightly so far this week, down 0.6%.

Retail sentiment on TLT and SHY was ‘bullish,’ with ‘high’ message volumes.

Yield Curve & Global Sovereign Markets 

Selling pressure rippled across international sovereign debt markets, following the path of U.S. Treasuries. Borrowing costs have again come under investor scrutiny, with many tech firms continuing to expand fundraising activities through open markets or institutional-grade loans.

The repricing was catalyzed by October consumer price index figures that outpaced economists' forecasts for the third consecutive month. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller publicly endorsed a potential half-percentage-point rate hike if inflation momentum persists, a sentiment echoed by Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan and Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee during the week.

"This is a tougher environment than during the Covid pandemic and the global financial crisis... Those were big directional moves – today it's about rolling supply shocks and wild rates volatility," Kellie Wood at Schroders told Bloomberg.

The market has now fully priced in the probability of the Federal Reserve hiking interest rates in December.

Meanwhile, the Dollar Spot Index logged its most successful weekly performance since early October. The index advanced 0.7%, touching its highest since May 2025 as foreign exchange traders priced in a more aggressive Federal Reserve policy path.

Nvidia tips Arm Holdings CEO Haas to take over Jensen Huang's job, musk backs Huang's reinstatement
data.description:
California, Nov. 14 -- Nvidia's board has approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor to Jensen Huang following the latter's resignation as the chipmaker's CEO amid a controversy surrounding his alleged extramarital relationships, the Financial Times reported.

According to the Financial Times, citing people familiar with the matter, Haas, who has headed the SoftBank-backed British chipmaker since 2022, is among the names being considered by Nvidia's board as it explores leadership options following Huang's departure.

Haas previously worked at Nvidia for around seven years more than a decade ago and is understood to maintain strong professional relationships with Huang and several members of the company's board.

However, Nvidia has indicated that the succession process remains at an early stage. In a statement, the company's board said it was "in the process of selecting a search firm" to identify a new chief executive and had not "formally engaged" with any candidates, the Financial Times reported.

"Any speculation regarding individual candidates, whether internal or external, is premature," the board added.

The announcement comes amidst speculation that several Nvidia employees have started a petition to reinstate Huang, a move that recieved the backing of SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

In a post on X where he was replying to an X user, Musk said, "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too."

Jensen Huang announced his resignation on Thursday after 33 years at the helm of the company. Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is currently serving as interim CEO.

Huang's departure came amid mounting scrutiny over reports of his alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom some US intelligence officials suspect of having links to Chinese intelligence services.

The controversy had earlier intensified following reports of another alleged relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, who reports to Huang.

Reuters, citing two people familiar with the matter, also reported that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second company employee, adding to the scrutiny surrounding his personal conduct and leadership.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, transformed the company into one of the world's leading suppliers of artificial intelligence chips and became one of the most prominent figures in the global AI industry.

data.title: More Than 10,000 Flights Delayed or Canceled in FAA's Nationwide Groundstop— WSJ
data.description:
By Andrew Tangel, Jacob Passy and Alison Sider

The Federal Aviation Administration halted departing flights nationwide Friday afternoon, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns after air-traffic control communications were disrupted.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wrote on X that there had been a communication issue affecting multiple air route traffic-control centers, which handle high-altitude flights covering large swaths of the country. "FAA technicians are investigating the issue," he wrote.

Planes in the air are able to continue flying to their destinations, an FAA spokeswoman said. Inbound international flights will be managed on a case-by-case basis, the agency said.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House on Friday that "there was no prior indication, or indication as of yet, that this was a nefarious attack against us. This is a telecommunications outage as of now." When asked if it could be a cyberattack, Mullin said officials weren't ruling anything out yet.

"There's no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones," Mullin said.

The groundstop started Friday afternoon at 3:53 p.m. ET. More than 3,300 U.S. flights had been canceled and more than 10,200 had been delayed as of Friday at 6:40 p.m. ET, according to FlightAware. Airlines also started scrubbing weekend flights, with more than 300 canceled on Saturday.

Disruptions are likely to grow. With departures halted, airports fill up, leaving little room for more flights to land. Nearly 500 flights returned to the airport they took off from as of 5:50 pm ET Friday, and more than 100 diverted to another airport, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics firm.

That leaves planes and crew members out of place for their next flights, which could create cascading scheduling problems into the weekend.

Some international departures from the east and west coasts were being allowed to take off Friday evening, according to industry officials.

At Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, word quickly spread among travelers while ground traffic appeared to suddenly stop on the tarmac late Friday afternoon. By early evening, telecom issues at some FAA air-traffic facilities were coming back online, according to people familiar with the matter.

The outage appears to be affecting a telecommunications network overseen by L3Harris Technologies, according to people briefed on the matter. The network handles crucial radio frequencies that air-traffic controllers use to communicate with pilots, the people said. It wasn't immediately clear whether the outage also affected the radar feeds that controllers use to keep aircraft safely separated in the skies.

An L3Harris spokeswoman didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

United Airlines said it is responding to the groundstop and will work with customers to get them to destinations once the issue is resolved. American said it expects its schedule to be disrupted for the rest of the day, depending how long the groundstop remains in place.

"It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop," American said in a statement.

Several airlines issued waivers to allow travelers to rebook flights without penalty. At some airports, including New York's LaGuardia, travelers whose flights were cancelled had to wait in long lines to get their checked bags back before they could go home. At Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey, security lines were empty as people milled about checking their phones for updates.

John Sturino, a musician who plays the drums, said he is going to miss a percussion convention in Indianapolis because of the flight delay. The Brooklyn native said he had been waiting half an hour in line to cancel his flight at the Delta lounge desk in LaGuardia Airport and get a refund.

"It wasn't worth staying in the airport," he said.

Sara Garven, 66, was traveling with her husband home to Wisconsin from Sarasota, Fla., when the couple were stranded in Baltimore where they had a layover. Overhead announcements were being made roughly every 30 minutes, she said, but the information was no different from what was available online.

"Some are sprinkling the Friday the 13th component, which isn't really helping," she said. "Our main concern is just getting home safely."

This is the second time in recent years the FAA has taken the extraordinary step of halting all departures across the country.

In 2023, a nationwide groundstop was ordered amid an outage of the FAA's Notice to Airmen system, which provides critical information to pilots. That order lasted for two hours, contributing to more than 1,000 flight cancellations. Before that, the FAA had only taken that step on Sept. 11, 2001.

The nation's air-traffic control system has been beset by communications issues leading to radio and radar outages that have affected various FAA facilities in recent years. Earlier this year, flights at New York-area airports were halted when a contractor accidentally cut a fiber communications line in New Jersey.

Other outages that have affected the Dallas area, Upper Midwest and New York City area have been relatively contained.

data.title: U.S. Targets $1.2 Billion From Binance Hack—Where Is the Rest?
data.description:
The Binance hack recovery has reached a significant milestone: U.S. authorities say more than $1.2 billion in stolen cryptocurrency is subject to court-authorized seizure or restraint. But that headline leaves a much larger question unanswered: what happens to the rest?

The Justice Department’s November 12 announcement puts the broader frozen total above $2.7 billion following the October theft. Crucially, the $1.2 billion is included in that figure. Adding the two would exaggerate the recovery, while calling either sum customer repayments would go further than the announcement supports.

Separately, Binance says it has completed coverage of the affected assets, having committed more than $6.34 billion in company funds to source replacement tokens through market and over-the-counter purchases. Its update says withdrawals continue reopening in phases.

That is a distinct milestone: replacing assets from company resources restores backing without recovering the original coins from the attackers. The law-enforcement totals should therefore not be read as a measure of how much Binance has replaced for customers.

Binance hack recovery: three numbers, three meanings

The FBI attributes the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor actors and dates the theft to around October 29. Its alert values the stolen assets at more than $6 billion.

That is the starting point. The frozen total describes assets intercepted by government and private-sector efforts. The court-authorized figure identifies a portion covered by seizure or restraint authority. Those are stages of intervention, rather than three separate piles of money.

“We worked together to freeze this massive criminal fraud in its tracks,” U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro said in the DOJ statement.

The language matters because a successful interception is not the end of a recovery. Establishing control, resolving legal claims and determining how assets can be returned are different questions. The announcement gives no timetable for completing that process.

The trail runs through Ether and crypto’s trading infrastructure

The FBI’s October 31 alert said investigators had observed stolen assets being converted primarily into Ether. It warned of further laundering through decentralised finance and instant-swap services and published addresses associated with the operation.

Its appeal extended beyond large exchanges to THORNode operators, RPC providers, DeFi services and blockchain analytics firms. That breadth illustrates the problem: stopping a theft’s proceeds requires action across the routes used to move and exchange them.

Public ledgers can preserve a transaction trail without guaranteeing that every destination can freeze assets. Investigators need both visibility and a point where someone can act. A traceable transfer and a recoverable balance are not the same thing.

For readers following the numbers, a precise remaining-loss estimate would be premature. These are dollar valuations of crypto assets, and the authorities describe lower bounds. Without matching valuation times and complete balances, subtracting one headline from another produces an impression of precision the disclosures do not provide.

A separate operation exposes the human weakness

The same enforcement announcement addressed FaceStealer, a separate North Korean social-engineering campaign. The FBI’s dedicated account of the scheme describes attackers hijacking communication accounts, recording victims’ webcams and using convincing imposter video meetings to compromise new targets.

According to the bureau, that campaign caused more than $400 million in theft over 18 months. Investigators seized over 900 victims’ webcam recordings. Those figures belong to FaceStealer and should not be added to the Binance recovery figures as though they describe one incident.

The disturbing element is the use of familiarity. A message can arrive through a compromised account belonging to someone the target knows. Recorded footage can then make an imposter meeting look like a conversation with a trusted contact.

The FBI also warns that open-source developers and maintainers are being targeted. Access to a developer’s software repository can put downstream users at risk, extending the consequences beyond whatever cryptocurrency is on the initial victim’s device.

Why a blockchain audit is only part of the defence

The implication is uncomfortable for technically sophisticated users: recognising a face, a familiar username or a plausible work request is insufficient authentication. Verification needs a separate route that the suspicious conversation does not control.

A request to install software or change a device during an unexpected meeting deserves particular scrutiny. For teams, the useful question is whether one compromised employee account can reach both operational systems and valuable assets. Separating those permissions can limit the damage.

This is a different threat from a flaw in Bitcoin’s underlying software. BNC’s Bitcoin Core security disclosure coverage explains why identifying the affected layer matters. A sound protocol does not protect a user who grants an attacker access to a device or signing process.

What would make the next update meaningful?

The most useful follow-up would distinguish newly frozen assets from previously announced balances, identify progress toward final recovery and explain whether funds have actually been returned. A larger number alone may conceal very different legal and operational outcomes.

The Binance case shows both sides of crypto’s transparency: stolen funds can remain visible as they move, yet visibility does not automatically stop them. The recovery effort has established a substantial foothold. The unanswered story is how much of that foothold can become a completed recovery—and how much remains beyond reach.

For exchanges, the practical test is readiness before the next incident: knowing who can authorise a response, preserving records and maintaining contact with the services that might receive stolen assets. A recovery operation becomes harder when those relationships must be assembled after funds have started moving.

CALGARY, Alberta, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- High Arctic Energy Services Inc. (the “Corporation” or “High Arctic”) is pleased to announce that it has entered into a definitive arrangement agreement dated November 13, 2026 (the “Arrangement Agreement”) with Newport Capital Ltd. (“Newport”) pursuant to which Newport, directly or through a wholly-owned subsidiary, has agreed to acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of High Arctic (the “High Arctic Shares”) for cash consideration of $1.59 per High Arctic Share, subject to adjustment in accordance with the terms of the Arrangement Agreement (the “Transaction”). The aggregate base purchase price payable by Newport is approximately $20.2 million, subject to the adjustments described below.

In addition to the cash consideration payable by Newport, High Arctic shareholders (“High Arctic Shareholders”) are expected to receive, as part of the Transaction, a cash distribution by way of a return of capital and/or a dividend (the “Shareholder Distribution”). The Shareholder Distribution expected to be paid to the High Arctic Shareholders is expected to range from a minimum of $0.20 to a maximum of $0.30 per High Arctic Share. The final amount of the Shareholder Distribution will be determined by reference to High Arctic’s working capital at closing, as described below.

The Transaction will be completed by way of a statutory plan of arrangement (the “Arrangement”) under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) (the “ABCA”) and, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions to closing described below, is expected to close in December 2026, and in any event prior to February 28, 2027.

Simon Batcup, Chairman of the Board of Directors, commented:

“This transaction and additional cash distribution to shareholders represents the successful culmination of the Board of Directors strategic review and delivers compelling and immediate value to High Arctic shareholders. The combination of a significant premium to High Arctic’s recent trading price and the anticipated additional cash distribution provides shareholders with an attractive opportunity to realize the maximum value for their shareholdings while eliminating the risks inherent in pursuing our business plan.

This transaction also marks the beginning of a new chapter in High Arctic’s history, a story that began in 1993 and since spanned multiple countries and a diverse range of oilfield services delivered to customers around the world. The Board of Directors and Executive Management are proud of what High Arctic and its people have accomplished over more than three decades, and we are confident that, under its new ownership, High Arctic and its exceptional employee group are well positioned to build on that legacy and achieve continued success.”

TRANSACTION HIGHLIGHTS

Certain and Immediate Cash Value

  • The cash consideration of $1.59 per High Arctic Share represents a premium of approximately 19% to the closing price of the High Arctic Shares on the TSX on November 13, 2026, a premium of approximately 27% to the 20-day volume-weighted average trading price of the High Arctic Shares on the TSX for the period ended November 13, 2026 and a premium of approximately 77% to the closing price of the High Arctic Shares on the TSX on May 14, 2026 when the Board of Directors (the “Board”) initiated the strategic review described below.
  • The all-cash consideration provides High Arctic Shareholders with immediate liquidity and certainty of value, without exposure to the execution, market and commodity price risks associated with High Arctic’s stand-alone business plan.

Additional Return of Capital

  • High Arctic Shareholders are expected to receive the Shareholder Distribution, by way of a return of capital, in addition to the cash consideration payable by Newport. The final amount of the Shareholder Distribution will be determined by reference to the amount by which High Arctic’s working capital at closing exceeds the target working capital amount of $2,432,000 set out in the Arrangement Agreement and remains subject to the approval of Newport (acting reasonably) and the Board.

Certainty of Completion

  • Newport has represented that it has, and at closing will have, sufficient funds available to satisfy its obligations under the Arrangement Agreement, and completion of the Transaction is not subject to a financing condition.
  • All of the directors and officers of High Arctic, together with FBC Holdings Sàrl, a significant shareholder of High Arctic, holding in aggregate approximately 49.2% of the outstanding High Arctic Shares, have entered into voting support agreements pursuant to which they have agreed to vote in favour of the Transaction.

RATIONALE FOR THE TRANSACTION

The transaction and additional cash distribution to shareholders provides compelling value relative to the strategic alternatives available to the Corporation. Since completing its corporate reorganization in 2024, High Arctic has actively pursued opportunities for accretive acquisitions in Canada to enhance shareholder value. However, the persistent and significant discount between the trading price of High Arctic’s shares and their underlying value has limited the Corporation’s ability to use its shares as acquisition currency and made it challenging to structure transactions that would be accretive to existing shareholders.

The combined total cash consideration expected to be received by High Arctic shareholders upon completion of the Transaction represents an attractive premium to the Corporation’s recent market trading price.

STRATEGIC REVIEW AND RECOMMENDATION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS

In May, 2026, the Board established a special committee of independent directors to conduct a strategic review, with the ultimate goal to recommend to the Board a broad range of alternatives to maximize shareholder value. The strategic review culminated in the entering into of a letter of intent with Newport on October 2, 2026 and the Arrangement Agreement on November 13, 2026.

The Board, after receiving the advice of its financial and legal advisors, and having received the Fairness Opinion (as defined below), has unanimously: (i) determined that the Arrangement is fair to High Arctic Shareholders; (ii) determined that the Arrangement and the entering into of the Arrangement Agreement are in the best interests of the Corporation; (iii) approved the Arrangement Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby; and (iv) resolved to recommend that High Arctic Shareholders vote in favour of the special resolution approving the Arrangement (the “Arrangement Resolution”) at the High Arctic Meeting (as defined below).

TRANSACTION DETAILS

High Arctic and Newport have entered into the Arrangement Agreement to effect the Transaction by way of a plan of arrangement under section 193 of the ABCA. Under the terms of the Arrangement, each High Arctic Share (other than those held by High Arctic Shareholders who validly exercise dissent rights) will be transferred to Newport, or a wholly-owned subsidiary of Newport, in exchange for $1.59 in cash, subject to adjustment in accordance with the Arrangement Agreement. Where the Transaction is completed through a subsidiary, Newport has unconditionally guaranteed the performance of that subsidiary’s obligations.

Purchase Price Details

The aggregate base purchase price of $20,191,499 payable by Newport is subject to downward adjustment, on a dollar-for-dollar basis, as of the effective date of the Arrangement to the extent that: (i) High Arctic has any outstanding indebtedness; (ii) High Arctic’s cash and cash equivalents are less than the minimum cash amount of $100,000 required under the Arrangement Agreement; or (iii) any High Arctic transaction costs are not expected to be paid and fully discharged by High Arctic as of the delivery of the final working capital statement (provided that High Arctic may instead elect to increase its minimum cash amount by the amount of such unpaid costs). High Arctic currently expects to repay and discharge its credit facility and mortgage financing, and to pay its transaction costs, prior to closing such that no adjustment to the $1.59 per share cash consideration is anticipated.

Shareholder Distribution

Prior to the acquisition of the High Arctic Shares by Newport, High Arctic expects, subject to the conditions described below, to reduce its stated capital and distribute an equal amount in cash to High Arctic Shareholders as a return of capital or issue a dividend or both. To the extent that High Arctic’s working capital at closing, as reflected in the working capital statement agreed between High Arctic and Newport, exceeds the target working capital amount of $2,432,000, such excess may be distributed to High Arctic Shareholders as part of the Shareholder Distribution. The Shareholder Distribution will not exceed the unrestricted cash available to High Arctic immediately prior to closing after reserving for all transaction costs, the required minimum cash and any other cash High Arctic is required to retain under the Arrangement Agreement. The Shareholder Distribution is subject to the approval of Newport (acting reasonably) and the Board, and to the receipt of all required corporate, shareholder, court, securities law, stock exchange, tax and other regulatory approvals.

Treatment of Stock Options

Immediately prior to the Arrangement, all outstanding stock options of High Arctic (whether vested or unvested) will vest and will be surrendered to High Arctic in exchange for a cash payment equal to the amount, if any, by which $1.59 exceeds the exercise price of such option, less applicable withholdings in accordance with the Company’s Omnibus Equity Incentive Plan.

Shareholder and Court Approvals

The Arrangement will require the approval of at least 66⅔% of the votes cast by High Arctic Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy at a special meeting of High Arctic Shareholders to be called to consider the Arrangement Resolution (the “High Arctic Meeting”) and, if required, a majority of the votes cast by High Arctic Shareholders, excluding the votes of persons required to be excluded under Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions. The High Arctic Meeting is expected to be held in December 2026. The Arrangement is also subject to the approval of the Court of King’s Bench of Alberta.

Conditions to Closing

In addition to the shareholder and court approvals described above, completion of the Transaction is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain other conditions customary for a transaction of this nature, including, among others: the approval of the Toronto Stock Exchange (the “TSX”); holders of not more than 15% of the outstanding High Arctic Shares having validly exercised dissent rights; the repayment and discharge in full of High Arctic’s credit facility and mortgage financing; the payment and discharge of all High Arctic transaction costs; the completion of the sale or other disposition of certain real estate assets owned by High Arctic, or the implementation of an alternative arrangement acceptable to Newport; and the absence of a material adverse change in respect of High Arctic.

Deal Protections

The Arrangement Agreement contains representations and warranties, covenants and conditions customary for a transaction of this nature, including a non-solicitation covenant on the part of High Arctic, subject to customary “fiduciary out” provisions that entitle High Arctic to consider and accept a superior proposal, and a right in favour of Newport to match any superior proposal within five business days of receipt of the superior proposal. The Arrangement Agreement provides for a termination fee of $1 million payable by High Arctic to Newport in certain circumstances, including if High Arctic terminates the Arrangement Agreement to accept a superior proposal or the Board changes its recommendation to the shareholders to vote in favour of the Arrangement Resolution, and a termination fee of $1 million payable by Newport to High Arctic in the event that Newport breaches its covenants in a manner that would reasonably be expected to materially impede completion of the Arrangement and fails to cure such breach.

Further Information

Further details regarding the Arrangement will be included in the management information circular of High Arctic (the “Circular”) to be mailed to High Arctic Shareholders in connection with the High Arctic Meeting. Copies of the Arrangement Agreement and the Circular will be filed on High Arctic’s SEDAR+ profile and will be available for viewing at www.sedarplus.ca. Following completion of the Arrangement, the High Arctic Shares are expected to be delisted from the TSX and High Arctic is expected to apply to cease to be a reporting issuer under applicable Canadian securities laws.

FINANCIAL ADVISORS, FAIRNESS OPINION AND LEGAL COUNSEL

ATB Cormark Capital Markets is acting as financial advisor to High Arctic. Sayer Energy Advisors has provided an opinion to the Board (the “Fairness Opinion”) to the effect that, as of the date of such opinion and based upon and subject to the assumptions, limitations and qualifications set forth therein, the consideration to be received by High Arctic Shareholders under the Arrangement is fair, from a financial point of view, to High Arctic Shareholders. DLA Piper (Canada) LLP is acting as legal counsel to High Arctic. Burnet, Duckworth & Palmer LLP is acting as legal counsel to Newport and Gowling WLG is acting as special tax counsel to Newport.

About High Arctic Energy Services

High Arctic is an energy services provider. High Arctic provides pressure control equipment and equipment supporting the high-pressure stimulation of oil and gas wells and other oilfield equipment ‎on a rental basis to exploration and production companies, from its bases in Whitecourt and Red Deer, Alberta‎. Additionally, High Arctic maintains a minority equity interest in Team Snubbing, a leading provider of well-control services to the oil and gas drilling industry with operations in Western Canada and Alaska, US. The High Arctic Shares trade on the TSX under the symbol “HWO”.

Currency

All amounts in this Press Release are denominated in Canadian dollars, unless otherwise indicated.

data.title: Rubio assails international court in speech to conservative legal group
data.description:
Key points:
  • US sanctions on ICC take effect in April unless supporters reach agreement with Washington
  • Rubio suggests US would respond with force if ICC tried to enforce rulings against Americans
  • Curbing Iran's nuclear ambitions is central to war, Rubio says

By Simon Lewis

Secretary of State Marco Rubio attacked the International Criminal Court in a speech to a conservative legal group on Friday, arguing for a muscular foreign policy and against international law restraining US actions.

Rubio's speech to the Federalist Society in Washington, his first prepared remarks since Republicans were routed in the midterm elections on November 3, heightens speculation over whether he will leave his roles as national security adviser and top US diplomat to run for president in 2028.

Rubio, who has at times sought to provide an intellectual justification for President Donald Trump's "America First" foreign policy, has firmly denied reports he will soon embark on a presidential campaign, but the Federalist Society is an occasional stop for Republican hopefuls.

He has dismissed criticisms that the Trump administration has broken international law by such actions as seizing Venezuelan then-President Nicolas Maduro and striking boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific that it says were carrying drugs.

In his speech, Rubio said the goal of the US-Israeli war against Iran was to prevent Tehran from ever developing a nuclear weapon, which he said was particularly urgent because the Islamic Republic's "radical Shia clerics" had an "expansionist mentality."

He contrasted this with the government of North Korea's Kim Jong Un, whom Trump has met three times. "I'm not excusing the terrible things that have happened there," Rubio said of North Korea. "I'm just saying he (Kim) is not expansionist. He's not trying to invade Japan or, you know, China or whatever."

The US, Rubio said, would not “submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats,” repeating his assertion that the court would try to prosecute US officials or service members that he used to justify sanctions against the ICC announced last month.

“Americans have never agreed to submit to the ICC's authority, but that court and its allies in the global bureaucracy have appointed themselves judge and jury and executioner of the international order,” Rubio said.

The Trump ​administration has long been hostile to the Netherlands-based court, founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide, and has previously imposed sanctions on its prosecutors and judges. The ICC has received strong backing from most member states, which include all EU countries and all members of the NATO alliance apart from the United States and Turkey.

Washington has denounced the court over arrest warrants issued for Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and ​an investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan, which the ICC says is "deprioritized."

The US sanctions, designed to stifle the ICC’s ability to operate, will take effect in April unless supporters of the Netherlands-based court can reach an agreement with the US to avert them.

Rubio suggested that if the court tried to enforce its rulings against Americans, Washington would respond with force. Quoting the Roman general Pompey, Rubio said the US response would be: "Stop quoting laws to men with swords.”

data.title: Democratic senators order Musk to preserve records over Ukraine Starlink access, WSJ reports
data.description:
Democratic senators have told Elon Musk to preserve all records related to SpaceX's restrictions on Ukraine's use of its Starlink and Starshield satellite services, The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing a letter.

Ukrainian forces say Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink, is vital for front-line communications and drone operations in their defense against Russian drone and missile attacks.

But in mid-October, Ukrainian officials complained that the service had been restricted without explanation or warning, limiting the military's ability to conduct complicated strike missions against Russian forces and slowing interceptor drones used to shoot down Russian attack drones.

"The October and November restrictions now raise the disturbing possibility that these vulnerabilities persist even within systems on which the U.S. government relies," Senators Jeanne Shaheen and Chris Coons said in the letter to Musk, the report said.

The lawmakers sought SpaceX's records since September 1, including all communications related to Starlink and Starshield in Ukraine as well as communications between Musk, SpaceX executives and the White House and Pentagon, the report said.

Shaheen and Coons said the restrictions raised "serious questions" about SpaceX's control over communications systems critical to national security and criticized what they described as “opaque decision-making,” according to the Journal.

Reuters reported in October that an order to limit Starshield service used by Ukrainian forces came from inside the White House. Secretary of State Marco Rubio later disputed that account, saying decisions on Ukraine's access to the service were up to SpaceX and Musk.

Later that month Ukraine said Starlink and Starshield were operating normally. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Thursday, however, that Ukrainian military units had again recorded disruptions to Starshield communications.

data.title: What we know about Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang
data.description:
Key points:
  • Singapore says Alice Huang left in February and is barred from re-entering
  • Justice Department has not reached conclusion on whether Huang spied for China, Blanche says
  • Alice Huang was in Chinese finance before emerging at Singapore's Megaspeed

By Wen-Yee Lee, Andrew Silver and Laurie Chen

Alice Huang had a long career in Chinese finance before later emerging as an executive in the global race for artificial-intelligence chips.

Known also as Huang Le, she was a top executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company that was an Nvidia business partner in the Asia-Pacific region. Her reported affair with Jensen Huang led in part to his resignation as Nvidia CEO on November 12.

Several news organizations, including the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal, have reported that US and other government authorities had suspicions that Alice Huang was spying for Beijing. In the spring of 2026, Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the drafting of a classified memo detailing intelligence indicating that China’s Ministry of State Security had recruited Huang to target Nvidia’s CEO, the New York Times said.

Reuters has not been able to verify any of the allegations made in the New York Times, along with other media reports, about Huang's suspected spying for China.

Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy. Reuters attempts to reach Alice Huang have been unsuccessful. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are not related.

Here are more details about what is known about Alice Huang:

SUSPICIONS OF SPYING, GOVERNMENT STATEMENTS

The New York Times reported on November 10 that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had briefed President Donald Trump aboard Air Force One en ​route to China in May about US intelligence indicating Jensen Huang was involved with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy.

The briefing marked at least the second time in seven months that Trump had been told about the intelligence, the Times ​reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter. Reuters was not able to confirm these warnings to Trump.

President Trump said on November 9 that the FBI was looking into the spying allegations. He said Jensen Huang told him he had no idea of the spying allegations, and also said he did not need to act on intelligence when he was briefed.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on November 12 that the Department of Justice had not yet reached a conclusion as to whether Alice Huang was a spy for China. CNN reported that day that US intelligence officials are still working to understand their relationship, citing people who say there is disagreement about the strength of the evidence that she was recruited to spy for Beijing.

Singapore's home affairs ministry said on November 12 that it had seized Alice Huang's passport in 2025 while investigating her for other offenses, including buying servers that were exported via Singapore to Malaysia without entering the Singapore market. The ministry said there was insufficient evidence to establish Alice Huang had committed any offenses.

The country's foreign ministry also said it received "limited" help from the US in its probe that began in 2025 into false declarations in the purchase of servers and other related offenses. Alice Huang left the country in February and was barred from re-entering following Singapore's investigation, the ministry said.

TIES TO JENSEN HUANG

The Financial Times reported on November 6 that Alice Huang had a romantic affair with Jensen Huang. On November 8, Jensen Huang released a statement acknowledging an extramarital affair, without naming Alice Huang in the statement.

Reuters has verified photos of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang together at several different events over the last two-plus years, with the earliest dating to December 2023.

ROLE AT MEGASPEED

Huang became the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed International in March 2023, according to Washington-based research group C4ADS, which reviewed corporate records.

In October 2025, the New York Times reported the company was under US investigation over whether it was helping Chinese customers obtain advanced Nvidia chips subject to Washington's export controls. China has denied this allegation, and there has been no public finding that Megaspeed violated ​the rules.

Earlier this week, The Information reported that Jensen Huang's ties to Alice Huang facilitated at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chip sales to China.

Megaspeed said on November 12 that it has cooperated with US inspections.

CORPORATE ROLES

Alice Huang previously worked in banking and investment management, according to Chinese fund-industry records and an indexed profile on private-fund database ​Simuwang, which also listed an earlier career in television journalism. She also held senior positions at Shanghai Hexi Investment Management, a Chinese investment firm.

She held senior roles ​at a Shanghai investment firm before her role at Megaspeed, according to financial records, corporate filings and company materials reviewed by Reuters.

data.title: What It Takes to Get Your Wings Delivered During a Football Game-Fast and Hot — WSJ
data.description:
By Isabella Simonetti | Photography by Andy Jacobsohn for WSJ

DALLAS — Wingstop is known for one menu item: chicken wings. Ordering them can require the work of 40 different services from Amazon.com's cloud computing arm.

For Wingstop, which saw almost 74% of its restaurant sales in its third quarter this year come from its app and online food delivery and pickup services, efficient technology is everything. Its use of Amazon Web Services shows how Amazon is growing the most important part of its business by selling customers ever more services.

Internal technical consultants from AWS, dubbed "solutions architects," work full time with Wingstop, a chain of more than 3,000 restaurants. Before Wingstop launched its loyalty program called Club Wingstop earlier this year, AWS stress-tested the system with huge volumes of simulated traffic to make sure it would hold up on busy days.

During the Super Bowl, when massive volumes of orders for wings come in, a team of AWS engineers sets up a war room in Dallas to troubleshoot issues and ensure the ordering system runs smoothly.

"If they're not available for 10 seconds during the Super Bowl, there's a huge business loss," says Matt Wood, AWS's chief AI and technology officer.

It's a high-wire act. Last year, an AWS outage caused by a glitch with an obscure Amazon database disrupted life for millions of people across the U.S. It delayed more than 4,000 flights and stymied financial trades, Venmo transactions and the ability to send corporate Slack messages.

If something goes wrong with AWS, customers might not be able to order digitally at all, said Wingstop president and chief executive Michael Skipworth, sitting in a conference room named for wing flavor Brazilian Citrus Pepper in the company's headquarters. "It's a multibillion-dollar business going through those pipes."

Amazon is most famous for its sweeping e-commerce marketplace. But the company's profit engine is its cloud computing arm which works with government agencies and millions of companies including Netflix, Anthropic, Goldman Sachs, the U.S. Department of Defense and chains like Wingstop.

AWS generated $45.6 billion in profit in 2025, more than half of Amazon's operating income that year.

Increasingly, AWS is also fashioning itself as a trusted adviser for its business customers. In June, the company said it was investing $1 billion to embed engineers with clients to help develop AI systems.

On Amazon's most recent earnings call, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy, who previously led AWS, predicted it could "be a trillion-dollar-revenue business in the next five to 10 years."

Amazon was once seen as a laggard in AI, partly because it doesn't have a model on par with OpenAI's ChatGPT or Google's Gemini. But the growth of AWS has helped redeem the company in the AI race.

"They've been desperately trying to paint themselves as a leader in AI for years and have precious little to show for it, except for the part where they are, in many cases, the infrastructure all of that AI work is being done on top of," said Corey Quinn, chief cloud economist at Duckbill, which helps companies negotiate and manage their AI and cloud computing contracts.

An AWS spokesperson said staying focused on customers "has made AWS a clear leader in AI, and a big reason why AWS recently saw its fastest growth in nearly five years."

AWS has been integrated into the infrastructure of the restaurant business for years, especially through delivery apps and credit-card technology. Taco Bell, McDonald's and Starbucks all have technology systems that run on AWS. So do DoorDash and Uber. AWS powers the cloud infrastructure for nine out of 10 of the world's largest quick-service restaurant brands, Amazon said.

"No matter what size of restaurant, where you are in the world, there's a chance that some aspect of your eating experience touches AWS," says Deborah Matteliano Simeoni, AWS's worldwide head of restaurants and food technology.

The company is hosting sessions with clients to troubleshoot business problems and come up with AI-powered solutions. AWS is working with Wingstop to develop a chatbot that will help field issues with orders and eventually support voice-enabled ordering.

"We'll sit in rooms just like this and sometimes with wings and pizza or beer, and we'll just kind of brainstorm on what the really hard challenges are for that customer," says Wood. "What are the really needle-moving problems that they want to be able to solve from the business perspective for their own customers?"

Matteliano Simeoni, Amazon's lead on restaurant technology, travels around the country to help identify how businesses can use AWS's different services.

"My job is to eat, sleep, breathe restaurants all day and then understand the industry so well that no matter what's happening in the world, I can look at the set of 500 Lego blocks and have a point of view on what should be happening with them," she says.

A restaurant that specializes in chicken wings sounds simple enough. But Wingstop is facing recent sales declines. In the company's 2025 fiscal year, domestic same-store sales fell 3.3% from the prior year, and this year the company is predicting at least a 6.5% decline. Skipworth attributes the business woes to the fact that 55% of its restaurants in the U.S. are in areas that overindex to consumers who are under the most economic stress.

Additionally, the business model for Wingstop is one of extreme ebbs and flows.

Orders of chicken wings spike dramatically during National Football League and National Basketball Association games — so much so that the chain has to cook wings before they have even been ordered. Other times, wing orders drop off precipitously: Mango Habanero or Cajun seasoned 30-piece meals aren't the kind of takeout most people order alone for weekday lunch.

So Wingstop developed a machine-learning model that forecasts customer demands and runs on AWS technology.

"It's ingesting weather forecasts, school calendars, betting lines around games to gauge excitement factors," said Skipworth. "All this comes in and this thing operates at a level of precision that is scary."

Timing is critical. Customers want wings freshly made and piping hot. It takes 13 minutes for Wingstop to fry wings to perfection, both in terms of food safety and to ensure the skin texture is just right.

Until recently, the convergence of those factors could mean long wait times for chicken, especially during blockbuster sporting events when the orders pile up and the pressure is on.

"On a good day, it typically took a customer 20 minutes to get their order, which if you're going to live in the fast food, fast casual space is kind of an eternity," said Benjamin Newcome, Wingstop's director of applied AI and data science.

The chicken chain made a push to reduce ordering times. With an outside technology firm, it developed an AI-powered smart kitchen, which now runs on AWS.

The smart kitchen sends cooks — dubbed "bombardiers" — real-time information on how many batches of wings they need to drop into vats of bubbling oil before the orders are even in. A "wingman" sauces the meat in a medley of flavors, from lemon pepper to hickory smoked barbecue. The workers themselves aren't aware of which orders are forecast and which are from real customers.

Customers picking wings up in person can now get their food in about 10 minutes.

"The idea is if I can proactively cook ahead chicken to meet the upcoming demand that's going to come in the next 15 minutes," Newcome said, "I can have chicken ready and on hand, still hot and fresh."

data.title: The Next Wave of Food Inflation Is Coming — WSJ
data.description:
By Ian Hodgson, Konrad Putzier and Rebecca Cadenhead

Americans are straining under sky-high grocery prices. The pain might get worse.

Food costs rose at the fastest rate in six months in October, driven by snarled supply chains, unpredictable weather and, increasingly, high fuel prices because of the Iran war. The cost of restaurant meals rose at the fastest pace since December 2025.

And now, more farmers and big food manufacturers are preparing to pass higher energy costs on to consumers.

"The worst is yet to come," said Scotiabank economist Olivier Gervais.

At the Hunts Point Produce Market in the Bronx, N.Y., which distributes fresh fruits and vegetables to thousands of grocery stores across the Northeast, wholesalers have run out of room to shoulder rising diesel costs. "We absorb what we can, but a lot of it gets passed to the consumer because there's not a lot of margin," said Stefanie Katzman, the fourth-generation chief executive of S. Katzman Produce.

At food giant Kraft Heinz, CEO Steve Cahillane warned last week that price increases across its portfolio were coming in 2027. "The cost pressure is everywhere," he said, adding that while "the consumer is in a fragile state, there's clearly more inflation."

U.S. grocery prices in October rose 0.4% from the previous month, the Labor Department said Tuesday, ending several months of relatively benign food inflation. Prices of fresh food like fruit and vegetables increased at an even greater rate.

The sharpest hits landed on everyday dinner staples: Lettuce jumped 8% in October alone, while beef steaks climbed 1.7%, butter jumped 2% and cheese rose 1.3%.

The latest pickup in food prices comes as Americans are already struggling with stretches of elevated inflation as grocery prices soared by more than 20% in the years following the Covid-19 pandemic and have continued to climb since.

Food costs matter more to voters than other categories because groceries are a necessity. Those prices are also highly visible: Most Americans go shopping weekly. "Everybody feels them, even if they're small increases," said Bernhard Dalheimer, an agricultural economist at Purdue University. High food costs contributed to the sense of voter frustration that swept Democrats to victory in the midterm elections. In an ABC News poll of House voters, 59% of respondents said they were unhappy about grocery prices.

Food prices are volatile, and economists caution that one month's increase doesn't necessarily mean the costs will keep rising. Still, pressures are mounting as high diesel prices, freight surcharges and rising agricultural costs grind through production networks.

Crude oil prices have dropped from recent peaks, but the fuel that powers food distribution has stayed stubbornly expensive. Retail diesel prices have increased by more than 66% since the start of the war in Iran, reaching a record high of $6.53 in September.

The cost of transportation services has increased by 20% since the start of the year, according to the Labor Department, signaling that trucking and logistics carriers are passing elevated diesel bills down the line to wholesalers and processors. That pressure is already registering for distributors as wholesale food prices jumped 1.3% in October, the sharpest monthly increase in the producer-price index since February.

Fresh fruit is already costlier to import, a spokesperson for fresh fruit and vegetable distributor Dole said, as expensive fuel inflates shipping, fertilizer and packaging costs. Weather conditions caused by a powerful El Niño have only compounded the strain.

"Bananas cannot stay and cannot be sustainable at these prices, at this level," said fruit-and-vegetable distributor Del Monte's CEO Mohammad Abu-Ghazaleh on a recent earnings call.

Food-supply chains move slowly and sellers will eat higher costs for as long as possible before raising consumer prices, Gervais of Scotiabank said. While freight costs react immediately, the peak price impact on grocery shelves takes 12 to 18 months to fully filter through production and distribution markets.

"It's too early to say if pass-through has started," Gervais said.

The delay reflects the mechanics of producing and moving food, said Georgetown University economist Sharat Ganapati. Grocery chains often negotiate prices months in advance and retailers will absorb costs as long as possible before repricing.

"That will attenuate the immediate effect," he said, "but the pressure builds up."

Early cracks are already appearing in categories with short supply chains, where perishable goods can't wait out freight swings in cold storage. In October, consumer prices for fresh vegetables jumped 2.2%.

Farm-level costs threaten to compound the squeeze over the next year. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz also pushed up fertilizer prices because Qatar is a key producer. Prices are still elevated just as farmers are starting to buy for spring planting.

"This is something that could drive food prices over the next year," Dalheimer, the economist, said.

Campbell's chief financial officer, Todd Cunfer, told investors in September that the company raised prices across 60% of its product portfolio in a bid to manage rising costs. Previously, Campbell's had shut down two snack plants and cut more than 550 salaried jobs — roughly 13% of its corporate workforce.

But with manufacturers exhausting internal cuts and long-term contracts rolling over, the ability of retailers to shield customers from higher prices is wearing thin.

Lilia Vailikit, a 71-year-old retired nurse in South Florida, is already feeling the pain. She said she strains to make ends meet with her monthly Social Security payments, and it doesn't help that gas prices and her condo maintenance are also up. As a result of belt-tightening, she can no longer make trips to her native Philippines every year or two.

"Every time I go to the store, it's more expensive," she said. "Groceries — Jesus Christ."

Write to Konrad Putzier at konrad.putzier@wsj.com and Rebecca Cadenhead at rebecca.cadenhead@wsj.com

data.title: Biotech Dealmaker: Early-Stage Platforms And Tools Draw Capital As Full Buyouts Remain On The Sidelines This Week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Argenx (ARGX) agreed to acquire privately held Unnatural Products for $550 million upfront and up to roughly $1.15 billion in total value, contingent on development and regulatory milestones.
  • BioNTech (BNTX) agreed to purchase a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher from Scholar Rock (SRRK) for $205 million in cash.
  • Blackstone Life Sciences (BX) agreed to provide Pfizer (PFE) with up to $1.5 billion through 2028 to support development of berobenatide.

Immunology platforms and late-stage obesity programs drew the largest commitments, including private equity support, in a relatively quiet week for traditional biotech deals.

Large drugmakers and specialized investors continued to favor specific asset purchases and co-funding arrangements over outright buyouts of late-stage biotechs. The week’s biggest transactions focused on oral peptide discovery tools, an FDA priority review voucher and development financing for an existing GLP-1 asset.

Argenx Acquires Oral Peptide Platform For Up To $1.15B

Argenx (ARGX) agreed to acquire privately held Unnatural Products for $550 million upfront and up to roughly $1.15 billion in total value, contingent on development and regulatory milestones. The deal brings in-house UNP’s AI-guided macrocyclic peptide discovery platform, building on an existing partnership.

argenx plans to use the technology to develop oral or long-acting medicines for immune-mediated diseases, complementing its antibody franchise led by Vyvgart. UNP’s team and Santa Cruz site will continue operating as argenx’s dedicated peptide discovery hub, with deal closing expected by year-end subject to customary conditions.

BioNTech Buys Scholar Rock Priority Review Voucher For $205M

BioNTech (BNTX) agreed to purchase a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher from Scholar Rock (SRRK) for $205 million in cash. The voucher, awarded when the FDA approved Scholar Rock’s spinal muscular atrophy therapy ISEMBYLD in September, shortens FDA review of a future application from the standard ten months to six.

BioNTech intends to apply it to a filing from its late-stage oncology pipeline.

Blackstone Commits Up To $1.5B To Fund Pfizer’s Monthly GLP-1

Blackstone Life Sciences (BX) agreed to provide Pfizer (PFE) with up to $1.5 billion through 2028 to support development of berobenatide, the investigational monthly GLP-1 receptor agonist Pfizer acquired via its Metsera deal.

In exchange, Blackstone is eligible for milestone payments tied to U.S. approval of the monthly monotherapy for chronic weight management and certain sales thresholds. Pfizer retains full ownership and operational control of the program, which includes 10 ongoing or planned late–stage trials. The structure gives Pfizer more financial flexibility amid approaching patent losses for several of its blockbuster drugs, including Eliquis and Ibrance.

Charles River Buys Frontage Bioanalysis Operations For ~$470M

Charles River Laboratories (CRL) agreed to acquire Hong Kong-listed Frontage Holdings’ bioanalysis and Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics (DMPK) operations in Exton, Pennsylvania, for approximately $470 million upfront, plus up to $75 million in contingent payments. The deal covers two sites employing about 340 people and a CLIA-certified laboratory.

It expands Charles River’s clinical bioanalysis capabilities as part of a broader arrangement in which a consortium including Charles River is taking Frontage private. Deal closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

data.title: What Travelers Caught in the Groundstop Should Know — WSJ
data.description:
By Jacob Passy and Patrick George

Patrick McDonald had already boarded his flight from Los Angeles to New York. But they never took off.

As he deplaned with the rest of his fellow passengers, he went into problem-solving mode to salvage his business trip. But as he purchased a backup flight for Saturday, the price nearly doubled from $500 to $950. When he went to get assistance at a ticket desk in the terminal, he found it empty, meanwhile gate agents warned waiting travelers to grab food while they could.

"We're being told every flight on the runway has to evacuate — it's just taking a longer time because the ground crew is spread thin," McDonald said.

For stranded passengers like McDonald, being proactive is the name of the game. As of Friday evening, more than 13,500 flights across the U.S. were canceled or delayed. Airports from coast to coast filled with passengers waiting for word of whether their flights would ever get out — others were stuck on planes as gate space quickly became limited.

Amy Welton and Chuck Hawks were at the Newark airport rental car counter debating whether to rent cars and drive home to Omaha, Neb., and Phoenix, respectively. The two are co-workers who were in town for training.

Welton said she was in the boarding line when she started getting texts from friends asking about the groundstop. They were then told to leave the line and that an update would come at 6 p.m. Then, "Your update is we have no update," she recalled.

"I just want to go home," she said. "I don't want to sit in an airport and wait."

Here's what travelers should do if they are stuck on the ground now:

Put your phone to work

Lines at airline ticket desks, hotel concierges and rental-car counters are sure to be long. While waiting, whip out your phone.

Airlines including Delta, United and Alaska issued waivers to allow travelers to change plans without paying a difference in fare. Alaska Airlines said travelers could also cancel and get a refund. Delta was offering refunds in the form of credits for future flights.

The fastest approach will be to make use of the mobile app to request changes. Flights in the coming days will sell out, so the sooner you act, the better. Also consider reaching out to the carrier via X or other social-media platforms.

If you feel more comfortable talking to a real person rather than a chatbot, try to contact the airline via its international hotline rather than the domestic phone number, because wait times can be shorter.

Go into the conversation prepared with details for other flights you're open to taking, and avoid itineraries that include layovers to reduce the chances of more disruption to your plans.

If you can't make it to your destination in time for the reason you were traveling, ask airline representatives about the company's "trip-in-vain" policies. When triggered, these policies can provide you with refunds that might not be offered due to an extensive delay since the situation is beyond the airline's control.

Put your points to use

Most carriers have eliminated fees tied to redepositing points if you choose to cancel your plans, so using points or miles can be a good way of hedging your bets for backup flights. Keep in mind, refunds might not be possible for fares booked in basic economy, and make sure to cancel award tickets, which are booked using rewards, before the scheduled departure to get a refund.

Plus, using points can help you to save in the event that the cost of booking another flight or hotel is higher last minute.

Download airport apps

If you haven't done so already, make sure you have the app for your local airport saved to your phone. As hubs fill with passengers from delayed or canceled flights, airport authorities may advise those with departures later in the day to stay home.

For instance, at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey, security officers warned against going through TSA checkpoints because of the crowds on the other side.

Check with your credit-card company

Many premium cards come with travel-insurance benefits that can cover you for travel booked with that card. They may provide additional assistance beyond what an airline can do, such as booking seats on flights with other airlines or finding options for hotels.

If you plan to file any travel-insurance claims related to the groundstop, be sure to document any expenses. Take photos of itemized receipts for meals, hotels, ground transportation and anything else you might need to purchase as a result of the situation to get your money back.

Don't abandon your luggage

If the groundstop has caused you to rethink your travel plans entirely and you checked a bag, don't just leave the airport assuming your bags won't be flown to the destination.

Inform an airline representative of your plans, and ask them if your luggage can be pulled. If so, they may send it to their office near baggage claim where you can retrieve it. Or they may ask for an address the bags can be sent to.

If you have a flight tomorrow, prepare now

As of Friday evening, it wasn't clear how much of the snowballing flight delays would continue into the weekend. For those with flights in the days ahead, being prepared can prevent a lot of frustration.

In your carry-on luggage, pack food, a change of clothing and any essential medications to have on hand in case you're delayed. Make sure to leave your house with your phone fully charged — and have a way to charge it in the airport.

Write to Jacob Passy at jacob.passy@wsj.com and Patrick George at patrick.george@wsj.com
